sentences.l: And when I saw him, O my sister, I fell from the intensity of the fear.
sentences.i: When I saw him, my sister, I dropped down from sheer terror.
sentences.n: The duck is still telling her story to the peahen, and steps into it here as an eyewitness. The hamza in رأيته is the print's.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الشِّبْلُ فَإِنَّهُ قَامَ وَتَمَشَّى إِلَيْهِ وَلَا قَاعَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-shiblu fa-innahu qāma wa-tamashshā ilayhi wa-lā qāʿa
sentences.l: And as for the cub, he rose and walked to him, and no ground (?).
sentences.i: As for the cub, he got up and strolled over to him, and met him.
sentences.n: wa-lā qāʿa is doubtful: as printed it reads “and no ground”, which makes no sense here. Most likely the print has broken up wa-lāqāhu, “and met him”, with ع for ه; the print's letters and spacing are kept and pointed as they stand, and the idiomatic layer follows the likely sense. tamashshā, “to walk along, stroll”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَ إِلَيْهِ ضَحِكَ النَّجَّارُ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ بِلِسَانٍ فَصِيحٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣala ilayhi ḍaḥika al-najjāru fī wajhihi wa-qāla lahu bi-lisānin faṣīḥin
sentences.l: And when he reached him, the carpenter laughed in his face and said to him with an eloquent tongue:
sentences.i: When he reached him, the carpenter smiled in his face and addressed him in eloquent words:
sentences.n: ḍaḥika fī wajhihi, “laughed in his face”, here a friendly smile of welcome, not mockery. The shadda in النجّار is the print's.

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ الْجَلِيلُ صَاحِبُ الْبَاعِ الطَّوِيلِ أَسْعَدَ اللَّهُ مَسَاكَ وَمَسْعَاكَ وَزَادَ فِي شَجَاعَتِكَ وَقُوَاكَ
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-maliku al-jalīlu ṣāḥibu al-bāʿi al-ṭawīli asʿada allāhu masāka wa-masʿāka wa-zāda fī shajāʿatika wa-quwāka
sentences.l: O king, the majestic, possessor of the long reach, may God make-happy your evening and your striving, and increase your courage and your powers!
sentences.i: O majestic king, whose arm reaches far, may God bless your evening and your every venture, and add to your courage and your strength!
sentences.n: Rhymed prose (sajʿ): jalīl / ṭawīl, then masāk / masʿāk / quwāk. ṭawīl al-bāʿ, “long of reach” (bāʿ, a fathom, the span of the outstretched arms), means mighty and generous. masāk is masāʾak, “your evening”, with the hamza dropped as in speech; asʿada allāhu masāka is a greeting for the evening.

sentences.t: أَجِرْنِي مِمَّا دَهَانِي وَبِشَرِّهِ رَمَانِي لِأَنِّي مَا وَجَدْتُ لِي نَصِيرًا غَيْرَكَ
sentences.tr: ajirnī mimmā dahānī wa-bi-sharrihi ramānī li-annī mā wajadtu lī naṣīran ghayraka
sentences.l: Give-me-refuge from what has-befallen-me and with its evil has-struck-me, because I have not found for me a helper other-than-you.
sentences.i: Shelter me from what has come upon me and struck me with its malice, for I have found no helper but you.
sentences.n: The rhyme goes on: dahānī / ramānī. ajāra, “to give someone protection (jiwār)”, the sacred obligation to shelter a suppliant. dahā, “to befall (of a calamity)”. The shadda in وبشرّه is the print's.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ النَّجَّارَ وَقَفَ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ الْأَسَدِ وَبَكَى وَأَنَّ وَاشْتَكَى
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-najjāra waqafa bayna yadayi al-asadi wa-bakā wa-anna wa-ishtakā
sentences.l: Then indeed the carpenter stood between the two-hands of the lion, and wept and groaned and complained.
sentences.i: Then the carpenter stood before the lion, weeping, groaning and pouring out his complaint.
sentences.n: bayna yaday, “between the two hands of”, is “before, in the presence of”. al-asad, “the lion”, is the cub himself. bakā / ishtakā rhyme, with anna, “to moan”, between. The print writes يدى with final ى; the shadda in وانّ is the print's.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الشِّبْلُ بُكَاءَهُ وَشَكْوَاهُ قَالَ لَهُ أَجَرْتُكَ مِمَّا تَخْشَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-shiblu bukāʾahu wa-shakwāhu qāla lahu ajartuka mimmā takhshāhu
sentences.l: And when the cub heard his weeping and his complaint, he said to him: I-have-given-you-refuge from what you fear.
sentences.i: When the cub heard his weeping and his complaint, he said, “You have my protection against whatever you fear.
sentences.n: ajartuka, “I have granted you protection”: the perfect tense makes the promise binding the moment it is spoken. The hamza in بكاءه and the shadda in فلمّا are the print's.

sentences.t: فَمَنِ الَّذِي قَدْ ظَلَمَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-mani alladhī qad ẓalamaka
sentences.l: So who (is) the-one-who has wronged you?
sentences.i: Who is it that has wronged you?
sentences.n: The fatḥa on فمَن is the print's, marking man, “who”, and not min, “from”.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَنْتَ تَكُونُ أَيُّهَا الْوَحْشُ الَّذِي مَا رَأَيْتُ عُمْرِي مِثْلَكَ وَلَا أَحْسَنَ صُورَةً وَلَا أَفْصَحَ لِسَانًا مِنْكَ فَمَا شَأْنُكَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā anta takūnu ayyuhā al-waḥshu alladhī mā raʾaytu ʿumrī mithlaka wa-lā aḥsana ṣūratan wa-lā afṣaḥa lisānan minka fa-mā shaʾnuka
sentences.l: And what (are) you, you-are, O beast, the-one (whom) I have not seen (in) my life (one) like-you, and not finer in form and not more eloquent in tongue than you? So what (is) your affair?
sentences.i: And what are you, O beast? In all my life I have never seen your like, nor any finer of form or more eloquent of tongue than you. What is your story?”
sentences.n: The print has نكون, a misprint for تكون, corrected here. mā anta takūn, “what are you”, literally “what you are”, is a colloquial way of asking who or what someone is. The cub takes the man for some unknown animal: waḥsh, “wild beast”. mā raʾaytu ʿumrī, “I have not seen in my life”: ʿumrī, “my lifetime”, as an adverb, a spoken idiom. The hamza in رأيت and شأنك is the print's.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّجَّارُ يَا سَيِّدَ الْوُحُوشِ أَمَّا أَنَا فَنَجَّارٌ وَأَمَّا الَّذِي ظَلَمَنِي فَإِنَّهُ ابْنُ آدَمَ وَفِي صَبَاحِ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ يَكُونُ عِنْدَكَ فِي هَذَا الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-najjāru yā sayyida al-wuḥūshi ammā anā fa-najjārun wa-ammā alladhī ẓalamanī fa-innahu ibnu Ādama wa-fī ṣabāḥi hādhihi al-laylati yakūnu ʿindaka fī hādhā al-makāni
sentences.l: And the carpenter said to him: O lord of the beasts, as for me, (I am) a carpenter; and as for the-one-who wronged me, he (is) the Son of Adam, and in the morning of this night he will be with you in this place.
sentences.i: The carpenter said, “O lord of the beasts, I am a carpenter; and the one who has wronged me is the Son of Adam, and by the morning after this night he will be here with you.”
sentences.n: The irony is plain to the hearer: the carpenter is himself a Son of Adam, a man, and the cub does not know it. ṣabāḥ hādhihi al-layla, “the morning of this night”, is the coming morning. The shadda in فنجّار and the madda in آدم are the print's.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الشِّبْلُ مِنَ النَّجَّارِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ تَبَدَّلَ الضِّيَاءُ فِي وَجْهِهِ بِالظَّلَامِ وَشَخَرَ وَنَخَرَ وَارْتَمَتْ عَيْنَاهُ بِالشَّرَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-shiblu mina al-najjāri hādhā al-kalāma tabaddala al-ḍiyāʾu fī wajhihi bi-al-ẓalāmi wa-shakhara wa-nakhara wa-irtamat ʿaynāhu bi-al-sharari
sentences.l: And when the cub heard from the carpenter this speech, the radiance in his face was-exchanged for the darkness, and he snorted and snored, and his two-eyes threw-out the sparks.
sentences.i: When the cub heard these words from the carpenter, the light in his face turned to darkness; he snorted and growled, and his eyes shot sparks.
sentences.n: Stock phrases of rage: kalām / ẓalām rhyme, as do shakhara / nakhara, two sounds of snorting through the nose. irtamat ʿaynāhu bi-al-sharar, “his eyes threw out sparks”: irtamā bi- is “to throw out, let fly”.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَ وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَأَسْهَرَنَّ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ وَلَا أَرْجِعُ إِلَى وَالِدِي حَتَّى أَبْلُغَ مَقْصِدِي
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥa wa-qāla wa-allāhi la-asharanna fī hādhihi al-laylati ilā al-ṣabāḥi wa-lā arjiʿu ilā wālidī ḥattā ablugha maqṣidī
sentences.l: And he cried-out and said: By God, I-will-surely-stay-awake in this night until the morning, and I will not return to my father until I reach my aim.
sentences.i: He roared and said, “By God, I will keep watch this whole night until morning, and I will not go back to my father until I have got what I came for.”
sentences.n: la-asharanna, “I shall surely stay awake”: la- with the emphatic -anna after an oath. The shadda in لاسهرنّ is the print's.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الشِّبْلَ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى النَّجَّارِ وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنِّي أَرَى خُطُوَاتِكَ قَصِيرَةً وَلَا أَقْدِرُ أَنْ أَكْسِرَ بِخَاطِرِكَ لِأَنِّي ذُو مُرُوؤَةٍ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-shibla iltafata ilā al-najjāri wa-qāla lahu innī arā khuṭuwātika qaṣīratan wa-lā aqdiru an aksira bi-khāṭirika li-annī dhū murūʾatin
sentences.l: Then indeed the cub turned to the carpenter and said to him: Indeed I see your steps short, and I am not able that I break with your feelings, because I (am) possessor of chivalry.
sentences.i: Then the cub turned to the carpenter and said, “I see that your steps are short, and I cannot bring myself to slight you, for I am a creature of honour.
sentences.n: kasara bi-khāṭir, “to break someone's heart”, to hurt or disappoint them: a colloquial idiom, with khāṭir, “mind, feelings”. murūʾa, “manly virtue, chivalry”; the print spells it مروؤة, with the hamza on a waw, an old spelling kept here. The shadda in انّي is the print's.

sentences.t: وَأَظُنُّ أَنَّكَ لَا تَقْدِرُ أَنْ تُمَاشِىَ الْوُحُوشَ فَأَخْبِرْنِي إِلَى أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ
sentences.tr: wa-aẓunnu annaka lā taqdiru an tumāshiya al-wuḥūsha fa-akhbirnī ilā ayna tadhhabu
sentences.l: And I think that you are not able that you walk-alongside the beasts; so inform me, to where are you going?
sentences.i: And I do not think you can keep pace with the beasts. So tell me, where are you going?”
sentences.n: māshā, “to walk alongside, keep up with”. The print writes تماشى with final ى.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّجَّارُ اعْلَمْ أَنَّنِي رَائِحٌ إِلَى وَزِيرِ وَالِدِكَ الْفَهْدِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-najjāru iʿlam annanī rāʾiḥun ilā wazīri wālidika al-fahdi
sentences.l: And the carpenter said to him: Know that I (am) going to the vizier of your father, the leopard,
sentences.i: The carpenter said, “Know that I am on my way to your father's vizier, the leopard,
sentences.n: rāʾiḥ, “going”, the participle of rāḥa, “to go”, as in speech. al-fahd is the leopard or cheetah, here the lion-king's vizier. The hamza in رائح is the print's.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّهُ لَمَّا بَلَغَهُ أَنَّ ابْنَ آدَمَ دَاسَ هَذِهِ الْأَرْضَ خَافَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ خَوْفًا عَظِيمًا وَأَرْسَلَ إِلَيَّ رَسُولًا مِنَ الْوُحُوشِ لِأَصْنَعَ لَهُ بَيْتًا يَسْكُنُ فِيهِ وَيَأْوِي إِلَيْهِ وَيَمْنَعُ عَنْهُ عَدُوَّهُ حَتَّى لَايَصِلَ إِلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ
sentences.tr: li-annahu lammā balaghahu anna ibna Ādama dāsa hādhihi al-arḍa khāfa ʿalā nafsihi khawfan ʿaẓīman wa-arsala ilayya rasūlan mina al-wuḥūshi li-aṣnaʿa lahu baytan yaskunu fīhi wa-yaʾwī ilayhi wa-yamnaʿu ʿanhu ʿaduwwahu ḥattā lā yaṣila ilayhi aḥadun min banī Ādama
sentences.l: because he, when it reached him that the Son of Adam had trodden this land, feared for himself a great fear, and sent to me a messenger from the beasts so-that I make for him a house he may dwell in and take-shelter in, and (that) keeps from him his enemy, so-that not reaches him anyone of the sons of Adam.
sentences.i: because when he heard that the Son of Adam had set foot in this land he was gravely afraid for himself, and sent me a messenger from among the beasts, bidding me build him a house to live in and shelter in, one that will keep his enemy away from him so that none of the sons of Adam can reach him.
sentences.n: khāfa ʿalā nafsihi, “to fear for oneself”. khawfan ʿaẓīman, “a great fear”: the verb's own noun repeated as an intensifier. ḥattā here is “so that”, with the verb in the subjunctive. The print runs lā yaṣil together as one word, لايصل; the spacing is kept. The shadda in اليّ and عدوّه, the madda in آدم and the hamza in ويأوي are the print's.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَاءَنِي الرَّسُولُ أَخَذْتُ هَذِهِ الْأَلْوَاحَ وَتَوَجَّهْتُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jāʾanī al-rasūlu akhadhtu hādhihi al-alwāḥa wa-tawajjahtu ilayhi
sentences.l: And when the messenger came to me, I took these planks and directed-myself to him.
sentences.i: When the messenger came to me, I took these planks and set out for him.”
sentences.n: The shadda in توجّهت is the print's.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الشِّبْلُ كَلَامَ النَّجَّارِ أَخَذَهُ الْحَسَدُ لِلْفَهْدِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-shiblu kalāma al-najjāri akhadhahu al-ḥasadu li-al-fahdi
sentences.l: And when the cub heard the speech of the carpenter, the envy for the leopard took him.
sentences.i: When the cub heard what the carpenter said, he was seized with envy of the leopard.
sentences.n: li-, “for, toward”: the envy is directed at the leopard. The shadda in النجّار is the print's.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ بِحَيَاتِي لَا بُدَّ أَنْ تَصْنَعَ لِي هَذِهِ الْأَلْوَاحَ بَيْتًا قَبْلَ أَنْ تَصْنَعَ لِلْفَهْدِ بَيْتَهُ وَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ مِنْ شُغْلِي فَامْضِ إِلَى الْفَهْدِ وَاصْنَعْ لَهُ مَا يُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu bi-ḥayātī lā budda an taṣnaʿa lī hādhihi al-alwāḥa baytan qabla an taṣnaʿa li-al-fahdi baytahu wa-idhā faraghta min shughlī fa-imḍi ilā al-fahdi wa-iṣnaʿ lahu mā yurīdu
sentences.l: And he said to him: By my life, (there is) no escape (from it) that you make for me these planks (into) a house before that you make for the leopard his house; and when you-have-finished from my work, then go-on to the leopard and make for him what he wants.
sentences.i: He said to him, “By my life, you must make these planks into a house for me before you make the leopard his; and when you have finished my work, go on to the leopard and make him whatever he wants.”
sentences.n: bi-ḥayātī, “by my life”, an oath: bi- is the bi- of swearing. lā budda an, “there is no escape from…”, is “must”. ṣanaʿa al-alwāḥa baytan, “to make the planks a house”: two objects, the material and what it becomes. The fatḥa in فرغتَ is the print's, marking “you”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ النَّجَّارُ مِنَ الشِّبْلِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ قَالَ لَهُ يَاسَيِّدَ الْوُحُوشِ مَا أَقْدِرُ أَنْ أَصْنَعَ لَكَ شَيْأً إِلَّا إِذَا صَنَعْتُ لِلْفَهْدِ مَا يُرِيدُ ثُمَّ أَجِيءُ إِلَى خِدْمَتِكَ وَأَصْنَعُ لَكَ بَيْتًا يُحَصِّنُكَ مِنْ عَدُوِّكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-najjāru mina al-shibli hādhā al-kalāma qāla lahu yā sayyida al-wuḥūshi mā aqdiru an aṣnaʿa laka shayʾan illā idhā ṣanaʿtu li-al-fahdi mā yurīdu thumma ajīʾu ilā khidmatika wa-aṣnaʿu laka baytan yuḥaṣṣinuka min ʿaduwwika
sentences.l: And when the carpenter heard from the cub this speech, he said to him: O lord of the beasts, I am not able that I make for you a thing, except when I-have-made for the leopard what he wants; then I come to your service and make for you a house that fortifies you from your enemy.
sentences.i: When the carpenter heard this from the cub, he said, “O lord of the beasts, I cannot make you anything until I have made the leopard what he wants. Then I will come and serve you, and make you a house that will keep you safe from your enemy.”
sentences.n: The print runs yā sayyida together as one word, ياسيد; the spacing is kept. The print spells shayʾan as شيأ, an old spelling. The carpenter's reluctance is the bait: refusing makes the cub insist. The shadda in عدوّك is the print's.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الشِّبْلُ وَاللَّهِ مَا أُخَلِّيكَ تَرُوحُ مِنْ هَذَا الْمَكَانِ حَتَّى تَصْنَعَ لِي هَذِهِ الْأَلْوَاحَ بَيْتًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-shiblu wa-allāhi mā ukhallīka tarūḥu min hādhā al-makāni ḥattā taṣnaʿa lī hādhihi al-alwāḥa baytan
sentences.l: And the cub said to him: By God, I will not let-you go from this place until you make for me these planks (into) a house.
sentences.i: The cub said to him, “By God, I will not let you leave this place until you have made these planks into a house for me.”
sentences.n: khallā, “to let, leave”, followed directly by a second verb, mā ukhallīka tarūḥu, “I won't let you go”: colloquial usage.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الشِّبْلَ هَمَّ عَلَى النَّجَّارِ وَوَثَبَ عَلَيْهِ وَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَمْزَحَ مَعَهُ فَلَطَشَهُ بِيَدِهِ فَرَمَى الْمِقْطَفَ مِنْ عَلَى كَتِفِهِ وَوَقَعَ النَّجَّارُ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-shibla hamma ʿalā al-najjāri wa-wathaba ʿalayhi wa-arāda an yamzaḥa maʿahu fa-laṭashahu bi-yadihi fa-ramā al-miqṭafa min ʿalā katifihi wa-waqaʿa al-najjāru maghshiyyan ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Then indeed the cub made-for the carpenter and leapt on him, and wanted to joke with him; and he slapped-him with his paw, and he threw the basket from on his shoulder, and the carpenter fell, fainted-upon.
sentences.i: Then the cub went for the carpenter and sprang at him, meaning only to play; but he cuffed him with his paw, knocking the basket off his shoulder, and the carpenter fell down in a faint.
sentences.n: hamma ʿalā, “to make for, set upon”. laṭasha, “to slap”, a colloquial verb. min ʿalā, “from on”, a doubled preposition of everyday speech. maghshiyyan ʿalayhi, “fainted”, literally “covered over (with a swoon)”. The shadda in همّ is the print's.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ الشِّبْلُ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ وَيْلَكَ يَا نَجَّارُ إِنَّكَ ضَعِيفٌ وَمَالَكَ قُوَّةٌ فَأَنْتَ مَعْذُورٌ إِذَا خِفْتَ مِنِ ابْنِ آدَمَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-shiblu ʿalayhi wa-qāla lahu waylaka yā najjāru innaka ḍaʿīfun wa-mā laka quwwatun fa-anta maʿdhūrun idhā khifta mini ibni Ādama
sentences.l: And the cub laughed at him and said to him: Woe-to-you, O carpenter, indeed you (are) weak and you have no strength; so you (are) excused if you feared the Son of Adam.
sentences.i: The cub laughed at him and said, “Confound you, carpenter, how weak you are, with no strength in you at all! No wonder you are afraid of the Son of Adam.”
sentences.n: ḍaḥika ʿalā, “to laugh at”. waylaka, “woe to you”, here half scornful, half affectionate. The print runs mā laka, “you have not”, together as one word, ومالك; the spacing is kept. The madda in آدم is the print's.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَقَعَ النَّجَّارُ عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ اغْتَاظَ غَيْظًا شَدِيدًا وَلَكِنَّهُ كَتَمَ ذَلِكَ عَنِ الشِّبْلِ مِنْ خَوْفِهِ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waqaʿa al-najjāru ʿalā ẓahrihi ightāẓa ghayẓan shadīdan wa-lākinnahu katama dhālika ʿani al-shibli min khawfihi minhu
sentences.l: And when the carpenter fell on his back, he was-enraged a severe rage, but he concealed that from the cub out-of his fear of him.
sentences.i: When the carpenter fell on his back, he was furious, but out of fear of the cub he hid it from him.
sentences.n: ightāẓa ghayẓan shadīdan, “raged a fierce rage”: the verb's own noun repeated as an intensifier.

sentences.t: فَتَعَلَّ النَّجَّارُ عَلَى حَيْلِهِ وَضَحِكَ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ هَا أَنَا أَصْنَعُ لَكَ الْبَيْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿalla al-najjāru ʿalā ḥaylihi wa-ḍaḥika fī wajhihi wa-qāla lahu hā anā aṣnaʿu laka al-bayta
sentences.l: And the carpenter [rose] on his strength, and laughed in his face, and said to him: Here I am, making for you the house.
sentences.i: The carpenter got to his feet, smiled in his face, and said, “There, I will make you the house.”
sentences.n: The first word is doubtful: the print has فتعل, which is not a known verb. The sense must be “he got up”, since ʿalā ḥaylihi, “on his strength”, goes with verbs of standing up, as in spoken qāma ʿalā ḥēlu, “he got to his feet”. Perhaps a letter has dropped out, as in fa-taʿallā, “and he rose up”, but that is a guess, so the print is kept and pointed only provisionally. hā anā, “here I am”, announces what the speaker is about to do.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ النَّجَّارَ تَنَاوَلَ الْأَلْوَاحَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ مَعَهُ وَسَمَّرَ الْبَيْتَ وَجَعَلَهُ مِثْلَ الْقَالَبِ عَلَى قِيَاسِ الشِّبْلِ وَخَلَّى بَابَهُ مَفْتُوحًا لِأَنَّهُ جَعَلَهُ عَلَى صُورَةِ الصُّنْدُوقِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-najjāra tanāwala al-alwāḥa allatī kānat maʿahu wa-sammara al-bayta wa-jaʿalahu mithla al-qālabi ʿalā qiyāsi al-shibli wa-khallā bābahu maftūḥan li-annahu jaʿalahu ʿalā ṣūrati al-ṣundūqi
sentences.l: Then indeed the carpenter took the planks which were with him, and nailed the house, and made it like the mould, to the measure of the cub, and left its door open, because he made it in the form of the box.
sentences.i: Then the carpenter took up the planks he had with him and nailed the house together, shaping it like a mould to the cub's measure. He left its door open, for he had made it in the shape of a chest.
sentences.n: sammara, “to nail”, from mismār, “nail”. qālab, “mould, form”. khallā, “to leave”, as in speech. The “door” is presumably the open top of the box, the opening the next sentence calls a ṭāqa. The shadda in وخلّى is the print's.

sentences.t: وَفَتَحَ لَهُ طَاقَةً كَبِيرَةً وَجَعَلَ لَهَا غِطَاءً كَبِيرًا وَثَقَبَ فِيهِ ثُقَبًا كَثِيرَةً وَأَخْرَجَ مِنْهَا مَسَامِيرَ مُطَرَّفَةً
sentences.tr: wa-fataḥa lahu ṭāqatan kabīratan wa-jaʿala lahā ghiṭāʾan kabīran wa-thaqaba fīhi thuqaban kathīratan wa-akhraja minhā masāmīra muṭarrafatan
sentences.l: And he opened for it a large opening, and made for it a large cover, and bored in it many holes, and brought-out through them pointed nails.
sentences.i: He opened a large hatch in it and made a large lid for it, bored many holes in the lid, and drove sharp nails through them.
sentences.n: ṭāqa, “window, opening”. thuqab, plural of thuqba, “hole”. muṭarrafa is doubtful: taken here as “sharpened at the tip”, from ṭaraf, “tip”; the print may intend another word. The nails, pointing inward, are the trap. The hamza in غطاء is the print's.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِلشِّبْلِ ادْخُلْ فِي هَذَا الْبَيْتِ مِنْ هَذِهِ الطَّاقَةِ حَتَّى أَقِيسَهُ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-al-shibli udkhul fī hādhā al-bayti min hādhihi al-ṭāqati ḥattā aqīsahu ʿalayka
sentences.l: And he said to the cub: Enter into this house through this opening, so-that I may-measure it against you.
sentences.i: Then he said to the cub, “Get into this house through this hatch, so that I can fit it to your size.”
sentences.n: The print has اتيسه, a misprint for اقيسه, corrected here. qāsa ʿalā, “to measure against”, fit to size, takes up qiyās, “measure”, above.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الشِّبْلُ بِذَلِكَ وَأَتَى إِلَى تِلْكَ الطَّاقَةِ فَرَأَهَا ضَيِّقَةً
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-shiblu bi-dhālika wa-atā ilā tilka al-ṭāqati fa-raʾāhā ḍayyiqatan
sentences.l: And the cub rejoiced at that, and came to that opening, and saw-it narrow.
sentences.i: The cub was delighted, and went up to the hatch, but saw that it was narrow.
sentences.n: fariḥa bi-, “to be glad at”. The print spells raʾāhā, “he saw it”, as رأَها, with its own fatḥa on the hamza and without the long ā that رآها would show; the spelling is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّجَّارُ ادْخُلْ وَابْرِكْ عَلَى يَدَيْكَ وَرِجْلَيْكَ فَفَعَلَ الشِّبْلُ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-najjāru udkhul wa-ibrik ʿalā yadayka wa-rijlayka fa-faʿala al-shiblu dhālika
sentences.l: And the carpenter said to him: Enter, and kneel-down on your two-hands and your two-feet. And the cub did that.
sentences.i: The carpenter said to him, “Go in, and crouch down on your hands and feet.” And the cub did so.
sentences.n: baraka, “to kneel down”, is the word for a camel lying down; the sukūn and kasra in وابْرِك are the print's, which points the imperative as ibrik rather than the ubruk of the dictionaries.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ الصُّنْدُوقَ فَبَقِيَ ذَنَبُهُ خَارِجًا فِي آخِرِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala al-ṣundūqa fa-baqiya dhanabuhu khārijan fī ākhirihi
sentences.l: And he entered the box, and his tail remained outside, at its end.
sentences.i: So he went into the box, but his tail was left sticking out at the back.
sentences.n: ṣundūq, “box, chest”. fī ākhirihi, “at its end”: at the back of the box. The hamza in آخره is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَأَرَادَ الشِّبْلُ أَنْ يَتَأَخَّرَ إِلَى وَرَائِهِ وَيَخْرُجَ فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّجَّارُ أَمْهِلْ وَاصْبِرْ حَتَّى أَنْظُرَ هَلْ يَسَعُ ذَنَبَكَ مَعَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-arāda al-shiblu an yataʾakhkhara ilā warāʾihi wa-yakhruja fa-qāla lahu al-najjāru amhil wa-iṣbir ḥattā anẓura hal yasaʿu dhanabaka maʿaka
sentences.l: And the cub wanted to draw-back to his rear and come-out; and the carpenter said to him: Give-it-time and be-patient, until I see whether it holds your tail with you.
sentences.i: The cub wanted to back out again, but the carpenter said to him, “Wait, be patient, till I see whether there is room for your tail in there with you.”
sentences.n: yasaʿu, from wasiʿa, “to hold, have room for”: the subject is the box, not named, and the tail is its object. amhil, “take your time, wait”; the hamza of yataʾakhkhara and warāʾihi is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَامْتَثَلَ الشِّبْلُ أَمْرَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-imtathala al-shiblu amrahu
sentences.l: And the cub complied-with his command.
sentences.i: And the cub did as he was told.
sentences.n: imtathala amrahu, “he conformed to his command”, the standard phrase for obeying an order.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ النَّجَّارَ لَفَّ ذَنَبَ الشِّبْلِ وَحَشَاهُ فِى الصُّنْدُوقِ وَرَدَّ اللَّوْحَ عَلَى الطَّاقَةِ سَرِيعًا وَسَمَّرَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-najjāra laffa dhanaba al-shibli wa-ḥashāhu fī al-ṣundūqi wa-radda al-lawḥa ʿalā al-ṭāqati sarīʿan wa-sammarahu
sentences.l: Then the carpenter rolled-up the tail of the cub and stuffed-it into the box, and put-back the plank over the opening quickly, and nailed-it.
sentences.i: Then the carpenter coiled up the cub's tail and stuffed it into the box, swiftly set the plank back over the opening, and nailed it fast.
sentences.n: ṭāqa, “opening, window”: the hole through which the cub crawled in. sammara, “to nail”, from mismār, “nail”. The shadda on لفّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَ الشِّبْلُ قَائِلًا يَا نَجَّارُمَا هَذَا الْبَيْتُ الضَّيِّقُ الَّذِى صَنَعْتَهُ لِي دَعْنِي أَخْرُجْ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥa al-shiblu qāʾilan yā najjāru mā hādhā al-baytu al-ḍayyiqu alladhī ṣanaʿtahu lī daʿnī akhruj minhu
sentences.l: And the cub cried-out, saying: O carpenter, what is this narrow house which you made for me? Let me come-out of it!
sentences.i: The cub cried out, “Carpenter, what is this cramped house you have made me? Let me out of it!”
sentences.n: The print runs نجار and ما together as نجارما; the spacing is kept. akhruj is jussive, answering the command daʿnī, “let me”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّجَّارُ هَيْهَاتَ هَيْهَاتَ لَا يَنْفَعُ النَّدَمُ عَلَى مَافَاتَ إِنَّكَ لَا تَخْرُجُ مِنْ هَذَا الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-najjāru hayhāta hayhāta lā yanfaʿu al-nadamu ʿalā mā fāta innaka lā takhruju min hādhā al-makāni
sentences.l: And the carpenter said to him: Far-off, far-off! Regret does not avail over what has passed-by; you will not come-out of this place.
sentences.i: The carpenter said to him, “Too late, too late! Regret is no use for what is past. You will never get out of this place.”
sentences.n: hayhāta, “how far!”, an exclamation that a thing is out of reach: “no chance of that”. lā yanfaʿu al-nadamu ʿalā mā fāta, a proverb, rhyming on -āt with hayhāt. The print runs ما فات together as مافات.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ ضَحِكَ النَّجَّارُ وَقَالَ لِلشِّبْلِ إِنَّكَ وَقَعْتَ فِى الْقَفَصِ وَمَا بَقِيَ لَكَ خَلَاصٌ مِنْ ضِيقِ الْأَقْفَاصِ يَا أَخْبَثَ الْوُحُوشِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḍaḥika al-najjāru wa-qāla li-al-shibli innaka waqaʿta fī al-qafaṣi wa-mā baqiya laka khalāṣun min ḍīqi al-aqfāṣi yā akhbatha al-wuḥūshi
sentences.l: Then the carpenter laughed and said to the cub: You have fallen into the cage, and there remains not for you escape from the narrowness of the cages, O most-wicked of the beasts!
sentences.i: Then the carpenter laughed and said to the cub, “You have fallen into the cage, and there is no escape left for you from the straits of the cages, you vilest of beasts!”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: qafaṣ, “cage”, answered by its plural aqfāṣ. akhbath, “most wicked”, elative of khabīth.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا أَخِي مَا هَذَا الْخِطَابُ الَّذِي تُخَاطِبُنِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā akhī mā hādhā al-khiṭābu alladhī tukhāṭibunī bihi
sentences.l: And he said: O my brother, what is this address with which you address me?
sentences.i: “O my brother,” said the cub, “what way is this to speak to me?”
sentences.n: The speaker is the cub, not named. khiṭāb … tukhāṭibunī, noun and verb from the same root, “the speech you speak to me”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّجَّارُ اعْلَمْ يَا كَلْبَ الْبَرِّ أَنَّكَ قَدْ وَقَعْتَ فِيمَا كُنْتَ تَخَافُ مِنْهُ وَقَدْرَمَاكَ الْقَدَرُ وَلَمْ يَنْفَعْكَ الْحَذَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-najjāru iʿlam yā kalba al-barri annaka qad waqaʿta fīmā kunta takhāfu minhu wa-qad ramāka al-qadaru wa-lam yanfaʿka al-ḥadharu
sentences.l: And the carpenter said to him: Know, O dog of the open-land, that you have fallen into that which you used-to fear, and Fate has shot you, and caution has not availed you.
sentences.i: The carpenter said to him, “Know, you dog of the wilds, that you have fallen into the very thing you feared: fate has struck you down, and your caution has done you no good.”
sentences.n: kalb al-barr, “dog of the open country”, an insult. The print sets وقد رماك as one word, وقدرماك; the spacing is kept. Rhymed prose: qadar, “fate”, and ḥadhar, “caution”, with a play on qad … qadar. ramā, “to throw, shoot”: fate as an archer. The shadda on البرّ is the print's own.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الشِّبْلُ كَلَامَهُ يَا أُخْتِي عَلِمَ أَنَّهُ ابْنُ آدَمَ الَّذِي حَذَّرَهُ مِنْهُ أَبُوهُ فِى الْيَقَظَةِ وَالْهَاتِفُ فِى الْمَنَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-shiblu kalāmahu yā ukhtī ʿalima annahu ibnu Ādama alladhī ḥadhdharahu minhu abūhu fī al-yaqaẓati wa-al-hātifu fī al-manāmi
sentences.l: And when the cub heard his speech, O my sister, he knew that he was the Son of Adam whom his father had warned him against in the waking, and the voice in the sleep.
sentences.i: When the cub heard his words, my sister, he knew that this was the Son of Adam against whom his father had warned him when he was awake, and the unseen voice in his sleep.
sentences.n: The print has البقظة, a misprint for اليقظة, corrected here. yā ukhtī, “O my sister”: the duck is telling the tale to the peahen and breaks in to address her. al-hātif, “the caller”, a voice heard without a speaker being seen; here in a dream. Both abūhu and al-hātifu are subjects of ḥadhdharahu.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَيْضًا تَحَقَّقْتُ أَنَّهُ هُوَ بِلَاشَكٍّ فِيهِ وَلَارَيْبٍ فَخِفْتُ مِنْهُ عَلَى نَفْسِي خَوْفًا عَظِيمًا وَبَعُدْتُ عَنْهُ قَلِيلًا وَصِرْتُ أَنْتَظِرُ مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ بِالشِّبْلِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā ayḍan taḥaqqaqtu annahu huwa bi-lā shakkin fīhi wa-lā raybin fa-khiftu minhu ʿalā nafsī khawfan ʿaẓīman wa-baʿudtu ʿanhu qalīlan wa-ṣirtu antaẓiru mādhā yafʿalu bi-al-shibli
sentences.l: And I too made-certain that he was he, without doubt in it and without suspicion; so I feared him for my soul a great fear, and I went-far from him a little, and I became waiting what he would do with the cub.
sentences.i: And I too was certain it was he, beyond all doubt or question; I feared for my life with a great fear, drew back from him a little, and waited to see what he would do with the cub.
sentences.n: The duck now speaks of herself: she had watched the whole scene. bi-lā shakkin fīhi wa-lā raybin, a doubled formula, “without doubt or suspicion”; the print runs بلا شك and ولا ريب together, and the spacing is kept. khawfan ʿaẓīman, an absolute object: “I feared a great fear”. ṣirtu antaẓiru, ṣāra with an imperfect, “I took to waiting”.

sentences.t: فَرَأَيْتُ يَا أُخْتِي ابْنَ آدَمَ حَفَرَ حُفْرَةً فِي ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ بِالْقُرْبِ مِنَ الصُّنْدُوقِ الَّذِي فِيهِ الشِّبْلُ وَرَمَاهُ فِي تِلْكَ الْحُفْرَةِ وَأَلْقَى عَلَيْهِ الْحَطَبَ وَأَحْرَقَهُ بِالنَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾaytu yā ukhtī ibna Ādama ḥafara ḥufratan fī dhālika al-makāni bi-al-qurbi mina al-ṣundūqi alladhī fīhi al-shiblu wa-ramāhu fī tilka al-ḥufrati wa-alqā ʿalayhi al-ḥaṭaba wa-aḥraqahu bi-al-nāri
sentences.l: And I saw, O my sister, the Son of Adam dig a pit in that place, near the box which in-it was the cub, and he threw it into that pit, and cast on it the firewood, and burned it with the fire.
sentences.i: Then I saw, my sister, the Son of Adam dig a pit in that place, close by the box with the cub inside; he threw it into the pit, heaped firewood on it, and burned it with fire.
sentences.n: raʾaytu … ḥafara, “I saw (him) dig”: a past verb follows the object directly, without a joining word. ramāhu, “threw it”: the box, with the cub shut inside.

sentences.t: فَكَبُرَيَا أُخْتِي خَوْفِي وَلِي يَوْمَانِ هَارِبَةً مِنِ ابْنِ آدَمَ وَخَائِفَةً مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-kabura yā ukhtī khawfī wa-lī yawmāni hāribatan mini ibni Ādama wa-khāʾifatan minhu
sentences.l: So my fear grew-great, O my sister, and to me are two days, fleeing from the Son of Adam and fearing him.
sentences.i: So my fear grew great, my sister, and for two days now I have been fleeing from the Son of Adam, in dread of him.
sentences.n: The print runs كبر and يا together as كبريا; the spacing is kept. wa-lī yawmāni, “and to me (are) two days”, the usual way to say “for two days now”; hāriba and khāʾifa are feminine, agreeing with the duck. So ends the duck's tale.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ الطَّاؤسَةُ مِنَ الْبَطَّةِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿati al-ṭāʾūsatu mina al-baṭṭati hādhā al-kalāma
sentences.l: And when the peahen heard from the duck this speech —
sentences.i: And when the peahen heard these words from the duck —
sentences.n: The sentence breaks off here, cut by the dawn; the next night takes it up. al-ṭāʾūsa, “the peahen”, feminine of ṭāʾūs, “peacock”; the print writes the long ū on the hamza's seat ؤ, which is kept.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she ceased the speech allowed her.
